synoptic.summary: High pressure keeps the area dry and stable through Monday, with no precipitation or thunder in any launch forecast. Sunday and Monday a light flow from 160°–220° at 9–13 kt sits 2,000–5,600 ft above the landings. The launch forecasts keep flow from 140°–170° at the Point all day, so the usual afternoon switch to 320°–360° may not happen there, although the Salt Lake airport forecast still has it. On Tuesday a dry shortwave trough grazes northern Utah: flow aloft turns to ~300° and strengthens to 28–45 kt about 9,500 ft above landing, and mixing deepens to ~2,900 ft.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Building high pressure will bring stable conditions and a warming, drying trend to the region through at least Monday, with temperatures rising to 5 to 10 degrees above normal. On Tuesday, a dry shortwave trough will graze across northern Utah, producing a minimal drop in temperatures by a few degrees alongside 700-mb temperatures dropping to around 0C to +2C from around +5C on Monday.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure was 1025.6 mb at 16:54 Saturday, the same as 24 h earlier, with only the normal daily swing (1025.0–1027.6 mb). High pressure means a light gradient, so the local daily wind cycle should decide things through Monday.

observations.summary: Readings from 16:15–16:40 Saturday are current. All valley stations report the afternoon flow from 320°–360° at 7–13 kt, with gusts to 16 kt at Spanish Fork and 13 kt at Alpine and Lehi; Provo is near calm at 3 kt. That is stronger than the launch forecasts (3–4 kt, gusts 7–9). The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations.
